tools.meta_description: Create a PDF from your own text, free in your browser. Type or paste, then download a clean PDF with no sign-up.
steps: Type or paste your text in the 'Text for your PDF' box.
Press Create & Download PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, named ak-premium-created.pdf, to your device.

content.use: Create PDF turns plain typed text into a PDF file without any word processor or sign-up. A teacher types a short notice and downloads it as a PDF to share in a class group. A shop owner types a price list and sends it to customers. A student types an assignment cover note and attaches the PDF to an email. The text is set in a simple 12-point font and flows across pages, so long text becomes a multi-page PDF automatically. Everything happens in your browser, so the text you type never leaves your device. It is the fastest way to make a basic PDF when you only have words and no document software.
content.tip: Keep paragraphs short and press Enter twice between them so the PDF stays easy to read. If the text is very long, check the downloaded PDF once before you share it, because the tool wraps text automatically and does not show a preview first.
content.limit: The PDF contains plain text only, in one font and one size. It does not keep bold, italics, headings, images or tables, and it does not accept pasted HTML formatting. The text is set at 12 points and flows across pages automatically.
content.example: Typing a 3-paragraph shop notice of about 400 words and pressing Create & Download PDF gives a one-page PDF with the full notice in plain 12-point text.
faq: Can I paste text with bold or headings into Create PDF?
No. The tool takes plain text only and sets it in one 12-point font. Bold, headings, images and tables are dropped, so use it for simple notices and letters.
What happens if my text is longer than one page?
The text flows onto extra pages automatically. The tool adds pages as needed and downloads one PDF with all of your text.
Does Create PDF keep my text private?
Yes. The PDF is built in your browser with jsPDF. Nothing you type is uploaded to a server.
What file name does the PDF download with?
The file downloads as ak-premium-created.pdf. You can rename it after it downloads.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG, PNG and WebP images into one PDF for free, in your browser. No upload and no sign-up needed.
steps: Choose one or more JPG, PNG or WebP images with the file button.
Press Convert Images to PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has one image per page.

content.use: Images to PDF turns photos and scans into a single PDF file, one image per page. A student photographs handwritten notes and sends them as one PDF to a teacher. A shop owner photographs receipts and keeps them as one monthly PDF. A job applicant photographs certificates and attaches one PDF to an application. Each image is fitted to an A4 page with a small margin, so nothing is cropped. The images stay in the order you selected them. The PDF is built in your browser, so your photos are never uploaded anywhere.
content.tip: Choose the images in the order you want them to appear, because each image becomes one page in that order. For the sharpest result, use clear photos; a blurry photo stays blurry in the PDF.
content.limit: Only JPG, PNG and WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. Each image is placed on its own page, so you cannot put two images side by side on one page. Very large images are fitted to the page, not kept at full size.
content.example: Choosing 4 photos of handwritten notes and pressing Convert Images to PDF gives one 4-page PDF, with each photo on its own A4 page.
faq: Which image formats can I use?
JPG, PNG and WebP. Other formats, such as GIF or BMP, are not accepted by the file picker.
Can I change the order of the images?
No. The images are placed in the order you selected them, one per page. Choose them in the order you want the pages to appear.
Does the PDF keep my photos at full quality?
No. Each image is fitted to an A4 page, so a very large photo is scaled down. The result is a clean, readable PDF, not a full-resolution archive.
How many images can I convert at once?
There is no fixed count. Each image must be under 50 MB, and very large batches may run slowly because the work happens in your browser.

steps: Choose two or more PDF files with the file button. Each one shows a thumbnail of its first page.
Drag the thumbnails into the order you want the pages to appear.
Press Merge PDFs and download the single combined file.

content.use: People merge PDFs when a report, invoice set or application form is split across several files and needs to be sent as one document. A teacher merges chapter PDFs into one handout, a shop owner merges daily bills into one monthly file, and a student merges assignment pages before uploading them to a portal.
content.tip: Check the file order in the thumbnail list before you merge. Drag a file up or down if it is in the wrong place, because the merged PDF keeps exactly the order you see.
content.limit: Merged PDFs keep the original pages as they are. The tool does not flatten forms, remove passwords from a protected file, or fix a damaged PDF. A protected PDF must be unlocked first.
content.example: Merging a 3-page invoice, a 2-page delivery note and a 1-page cover letter gives one 6-page PDF in that order.
faq: Can I change the order of the PDFs before merging?
Yes. After you choose the files, each one shows a thumbnail of its first page. Drag the thumbnails into the order you want, then press Merge PDFs.
Is there a limit on how many PDFs I can merge?
You can merge as many as your browser can hold in memory. Very large files over 50 MB per file are refused with a friendly message, because the browser would run out of memory.
What file do I get after merging?
You download one PDF named ak-premium-merged.pdf. It keeps every page from your files in the order shown in the thumbnail list, and the original files on your device are not changed.
Can I merge just two PDFs?
Yes. Two files is the minimum. Choose at least two PDFs and press Merge PDFs, and the tool downloads the combined file.

tools.meta_description: Merge multiple PDF files into one PDF for free, in your browser. Keep your page order and download instantly.

short.en: Extract a page range into a new PDF.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick Page ranges, or Extract every page for one PDF per page.
Type ranges like 1-3, 5, 8-10, press Split PDF and download the result.

content.use: Splitting is for the opposite job: taking only the pages you need out of a long PDF. A student extracts chapters 2 and 3 from a 200-page book, a manager pulls one contract clause out of a full agreement, and a shop owner separates one month's invoices from a yearly file.
content.tip: Use ranges like 1-3, 5, 8-10 to take several separate parts in one go. The tool keeps the pages in the order you list them.
content.limit: Split pages keep their original content and formatting. The tool cannot split a password-protected PDF, and it does not rebuild text from a scanned page.
content.example: Splitting pages 1-3, 5 from a 10-page PDF gives a new PDF with exactly those 4 pages.
faq: Can I split a PDF into single pages?
Yes. Choose Extract every page and the tool downloads a ZIP file with one PDF per page, named page-1.pdf, page-2.pdf and so on.
What happens if I enter a page that does not exist?
The tool checks your ranges against the real page count first and tells you which range is outside it, so nothing is downloaded by mistake.
Can I take out just one page?
Yes. Enter a single page number, such as 5, in the Page ranges box. The tool downloads a one-page PDF with only that page.
What if my ranges overlap?
Nothing goes wrong. Pages listed twice are kept once, and the result is always in page order, even if you typed the ranges out of order.

tools.meta_description: Split a PDF and extract only the page range you need, free in your browser. No upload, no sign-up.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Drag the page thumbnails into the order you want. Use Rotate 90 on a sideways page and Delete on a blank page.
Press Download and save the organised PDF.

content.use: Organizing a PDF is for fixing page order after scanning or merging: a scanned book with two pages swapped, a report with the appendix in the wrong place, or a set of pages that were merged in the wrong order. It is also how you delete a blank or duplicate page.
content.tip: Drag the page thumbnails into the order you want. Use Rotate 90 on a page that was scanned sideways, and Delete on a blank or duplicate page, before you download.
content.limit: Organizing reorders, rotates and deletes pages. It does not edit the text or images on a page, and it cannot split one page into two.
content.example: Moving page 3 to the front of a 5-page PDF, rotating page 2, and deleting page 5 gives a clean 4-page file.
faq: Can I rotate only one page?
Yes. Each thumbnail has its own Rotate 90 button, so only that page turns. Press it again to turn the page further.
Do I have to type the page order as numbers?
No. Drag the thumbnails to reorder visually. Typing a number order like 3,1,2 still works if you prefer it.
Can I delete a page?
Yes. Each page thumbnail has a Delete button. The page is left out of the downloaded file, but you must keep at least one page.
Are my rotations saved in the downloaded file?
Yes. A page you rotated stays rotated in the new PDF. The rotation is written into the file, so it looks the same in any PDF reader.

tools.meta_description: Reorder PDF pages into a new order, free in your browser. Drag-free, simple page ordering with no upload.

short.en: Delete selected pages and keep the rest.

tools.meta_description: Delete selected pages from a PDF and keep the rest, free in your browser. Your file never leaves your device.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
In 'Pages to remove', type the page numbers, for example 2, 4-5.
Press Remove Pages and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Remove Pages deletes pages you do not need from a PDF and downloads the rest as a new file. A student removes blank pages from scanned notes before uploading them. An office worker removes a draft page from a report before sending it to a client. A shop owner removes an old price page from a catalogue. You list the pages by number, using commas and ranges such as 2, 4-5, and the tool checks every number against the real page count before it removes anything. Your original file is never changed; the result is a separate download.
content.tip: Type ranges with a hyphen, such as 4-5, and separate pages with commas, such as 2, 4-5. Count the pages first if you are unsure, because the tool refuses numbers above the real page count.
content.limit: You must keep at least one page; the tool refuses to remove every page. Page numbers that do not exist in the file are rejected with a message. The tool only removes whole pages. It does not delete text inside a page or fix a damaged PDF.
content.example: In a 10-page report, typing 2, 4-5 and pressing Remove Pages downloads a 7-page PDF with pages 2, 4 and 5 gone.
faq: How do I write a page range?
Type it with a hyphen, such as 4-5, and separate entries with commas, such as 2, 4-5. The tool removes pages 2, 4 and 5 in that example.
What happens if I type a page number that does not exist?
The tool checks your list against the real page count and shows an error, such as page 12 being outside 1 to 10. Nothing is removed until the list is valid.
Can I remove all the pages?
No. The tool refuses to remove every page and asks you to keep at least one page.
Is my original PDF changed?
No. The tool reads your file and downloads a new copy with the pages removed. Your original file stays untouched.

tools.meta_description: Rotate all PDF pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees, free in your browser. No upload and no account needed.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick an angle in the Angle list: 90, 180 or 270 degrees.
Press Rotate PDF and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Rotate PDF turns every page of a PDF by 90, 180 or 270 degrees, which fixes files that open sideways or upside down. A student rotates scanned notes that were photographed at an angle. An office worker rotates a sideways report so it reads normally on screen. A shop owner rotates a scanned invoice before sending it to a customer. The rotation is added to each page's existing rotation, so a page that was already turned 90 degrees becomes 180 degrees if you rotate it again. The result downloads as a new PDF and your original file stays unchanged.
content.tip: If a page is already rotated, remember the angle adds to it. A page turned 90 degrees once becomes 180 degrees if you rotate it by 90 again. Rotate once, download, and check the result before rotating again.
content.limit: The angle applies to every page at once. You cannot rotate a single page on its own. The tool does not straighten skewed scans; it only turns pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees.
content.example: A 5-page scan that opens sideways is fixed by choosing 90 degrees and pressing Rotate PDF, which downloads all 5 pages turned the right way up.
faq: Can I rotate just one page?
No. The angle you pick is applied to every page in the file. To fix one page, split the PDF first, rotate that part, then merge it back.
Why did my page turn 180 degrees when I chose 90?
The rotation adds to the page's existing rotation. A page already turned 90 degrees becomes 180 degrees when you rotate it by 90 again.
Does Rotate PDF change my original file?
No. It reads your file and downloads a new copy with the pages turned. Your original file is not changed.
Can Rotate PDF straighten a crooked scan?
No. It only turns whole pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees. A scan that is tilted by a few degrees stays tilted.

tools.meta_description: Add page numbers to every page of a PDF, free in your browser. Numbers appear at the bottom centre of each page.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Add Page Numbers.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has a number at the bottom centre of every page.

content.use: Add Page Numbers stamps a small number at the bottom centre of every page in a PDF, so long documents are easy to follow and refer to. A teacher numbers a 40-page handout so students can find the right page in class. A student numbers an assignment before uploading it to a portal. An office worker numbers a report so page references in a meeting make sense. The numbers start at 1 on the first page and count up in order. The tool adds numbers to the pages as they are and downloads a new copy, leaving your original file untouched.
content.tip: Number the final version of your document. If you edit the PDF afterwards and add or remove pages, the numbers will no longer match, so run the tool again on the edited file.
content.limit: The number is plain text at the bottom centre of each page, in a fixed 11-point font. You cannot change the position, size, colour or starting number, and the tool does not skip a cover page. Numbers are stamped on top of the page, so they may sit over a footer that is already there.
content.example: Adding numbers to a 12-page report downloads a copy with 1 on the first page, 2 on the second, and so on up to 12 on the last page.
faq: Where on the page does the number appear?
At the bottom centre of every page, in a small 11-point font. The position and size are fixed and cannot be changed.
Can I start numbering from page 5?
No. Numbering always starts at 1 on the first page and counts up in order.
Can I skip the cover page?
No. Every page gets a number, including the cover. If you need a blank first page, remove the number from that page with another editor, or split the PDF first.
Does the tool change my original PDF?
No. It downloads a new copy with the numbers added. Your original file stays as it was.

tools.meta_description: Stamp a diagonal text watermark on PDF pages, free in your browser. Your file stays on your device.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type the watermark text, for example DRAFT, in the 'Watermark text' box. Keep it under 60 characters.
Choose an Opacity and a Size, then press Add Watermark and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Add Watermark stamps your text diagonally across every page of a PDF, so readers can see at a glance that a document is a draft, a sample or confidential. A teacher stamps DRAFT on exam papers before sharing them. An office worker stamps CONFIDENTIAL on a report before sending it outside the company. A designer stamps SAMPLE on a portfolio file. You type the text, pick how faint or strong it looks, and choose a size. The watermark is a visible grey mark at a 45-degree angle, and it is stamped on all pages in one step.
content.tip: Use Light opacity for a faint mark that stays out of the way of the text, and Strong when the mark must be obvious. Keep the text short, such as DRAFT or SAMPLE, because long text is harder to read at an angle.
content.limit: The watermark text must be under 60 characters. It is stamped at a fixed 45-degree angle in grey, in the middle of each page, and you cannot move it or change its colour. A watermark is a visible mark only. It does not password-protect the file or stop someone from copying the text.
content.example: Typing CONFIDENTIAL, choosing Medium opacity and pressing Add Watermark stamps CONFIDENTIAL diagonally on every page of a 6-page report.
faq: Can I move the watermark to a corner?
No. The watermark is always stamped diagonally across the middle of each page at a 45-degree angle. Only the text, opacity and size can be changed.
How long can the watermark text be?
Under 60 characters. Longer text is refused with a message, so keep it short, such as DRAFT, SAMPLE or CONFIDENTIAL.
Does a watermark protect my PDF from copying?
No. It is only a visible mark on the page. Anyone can still copy the text or take a screenshot. For real protection, use Protect PDF with a password.
Will the watermark cover my text?
It may sit over text because it runs across the middle of the page. Light opacity keeps the page readable, while Strong opacity is more visible but harder to read through.

tools.meta_description: Add text to a page of your PDF, free in your browser. A simple way to stamp a note without installing software.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type the text in 'Text to add', then set the Page number, choose a Position and a Font size.
Press Add Text to PDF and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Edit PDF adds a line of text to one page of a PDF, which is handy for small fixes such as a missing heading, a note or a date. A teacher adds a class name to the first page of a handout. An office worker adds 'Approved' to the top of a memo. A student adds a title to the first page of an assignment. You pick the page number and choose where the text goes: top left, top centre, bottom centre or centre of the page. The text is added in a plain dark font, and the rest of the page is left exactly as it was.
content.tip: Check the page count before you type a page number, because the tool refuses a page that does not exist. Keep the added text short, so it fits on one line at the size you choose.
content.limit: The tool adds new text only. It cannot edit or delete text that is already in the PDF, and it cannot move existing content. The added text goes on one page at a time, in a plain font at 12, 18, 24 or 36 points. If the text is too long for the page width, it may run off the edge.
content.example: Adding the text 'Class 10-A' to page 1 at the top centre in size 24 puts a clear heading on the first page of a handout.
faq: Can I edit text that is already in the PDF?
No. Edit PDF only adds new text on top of a page. It cannot change or delete existing text, so fix typos in the original document and export a fresh PDF.
Which positions can I choose?
Top left, top centre, bottom centre or centre of the page. Pick the position from the Position list before pressing Add Text to PDF.
What if the page I type is not in the PDF?
The tool shows a message telling you how many pages the PDF has and asks you to choose a page inside that range.
Can I add text to several pages at once?
No. Each run adds text to one page only. Repeat the steps for each page you need to mark.

short.en: Reduce PDF file size (Light, Medium or Strong).

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick a level: Light keeps text selectable, Medium re-encodes pages as images, Strong makes the smallest file but text is not selectable.
Set the quality if you want, press Compress PDF and download the result.

content.use: A PDF that is too large to email or upload is the usual reason to compress one. Admission forms, job applications and WhatsApp forwards often have a file-size limit, and a compressed copy is what gets through. Compressing also helps when a PDF is stored on a phone with little free space.
content.tip: Start with Light if the PDF is mostly text. Use Medium for a PDF with photos, and Strong only when size matters more than being able to select or search the text.
content.limit: Light re-saves the file and only helps a little on image-heavy PDFs. Medium and Strong turn pages into images, so text on those pages is no longer selectable or searchable. Compression cannot fix a damaged PDF.
content.example: A 12 MB scanned PDF with photos often drops to about 4 MB on Medium and under 2 MB on Strong, depending on the images.
faq: Why is my compressed PDF still large?
Image-heavy PDFs compress by re-encoding the images. If the images are already small or the PDF is mostly vector graphics, there is little left to save, and Light may only remove a few kilobytes.
Does Strong compression change my text?
Yes. Strong renders each page as an image, so the text becomes part of the picture. You can still read it, but you cannot select, copy or search it. Use Light or Medium if you need selectable text.
What does the Quality slider change?
It sets the image quality for Medium and Strong, which turn pages into pictures. Light ignores the slider, because it only re-saves the file.
How do I know how much was saved?
The result line shows the old size and the new size, with the percentage saved. If the file grew instead, it says how much larger it is.

tools.meta_description: Compress a PDF and reduce its file size, free in your browser. Best for text PDFs; image-heavy files compress less.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Extract Text.
Save the downloaded .txt file, which lists the text page by page.
tools.meta_description: Extract text from a PDF into a .txt file, free in your browser. Works on PDFs that already have a text layer.

content.use: PDF to Text pulls the words out of a PDF and saves them as a plain .txt file, so you can reuse the text in a document, an email or a search. A student extracts a chapter to quote in an essay. An office worker extracts a report to paste figures into a spreadsheet. A researcher extracts several papers to search them together. The text is grouped by page, with a '--- Page N ---' marker before each page, so you can always tell where a line came from. The work happens in your browser and the original PDF is never changed.
content.tip: If the result is empty or garbled, the PDF is probably a scan with no text layer. Use OCR PDF first to read the pages, then extract text from the new PDF. Copy the text into your document and check the line breaks before you use it.
content.limit: The tool only reads PDFs that already have a text layer. A scanned-image PDF with no text layer gives no text, and the tool says so. Tables, columns and layout are not preserved; the text comes out as plain lines in reading order.
content.example: Extracting text from a 4-page report downloads ak-premium-text.txt with the words from all 4 pages, each page starting with a '--- Page N ---' marker.
faq: Why did I get an empty text file?
The PDF is probably a scan made of images, with no text layer to read. Use OCR PDF first to read the pages into a text PDF, then run PDF to Text on that file.
Does the .txt file keep the page layout?
No. The text comes out as plain lines grouped by page, with a '--- Page N ---' marker. Tables, columns, fonts and images are not kept.
Can I extract text from only one page?
No. The tool extracts the whole PDF at once. Open the .txt file afterwards and copy the page you need, using the page markers to find it.
What is the file called when it downloads?
It downloads as ak-premium-text.txt. Rename it after downloading if you want a different name.

tools.meta_description: Render PDF pages as PNG images and download them, free in your browser. No upload, no sign-up.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Convert Pages to Images.
Download each page PNG from the links shown, or download the whole set as one ZIP file.

content.use: PDF to Images turns every page of a PDF into a PNG picture, so you can share a single page in a chat, add it to a slide or post it online. A teacher turns one page of a worksheet into a PNG to share in a class group. A student turns a diagram page into a PNG to paste into an assignment. A shop owner turns a price page into a PNG for a social media post. Each page is rendered at one and a half times its normal size for a sharp picture. After the conversion, you get a download link for each page and one ZIP file with all the pages together.
content.tip: If you only need one page, download just that page's PNG link instead of the whole ZIP. Large PDFs take a while because every page is rendered in your browser, so wait for the status message to say it is done.
content.limit: Each page becomes a separate PNG, so a 50-page PDF gives 50 pictures and one ZIP. The PNGs are pictures of the pages, not editable text. A scanned PDF renders as a picture of the scan, which is fine, but a very large PDF may be slow or run out of browser memory.
content.example: Converting a 3-page worksheet gives three PNG links, page 1, page 2 and page 3, plus a ZIP file with all three PNGs inside.
faq: How do I download only one page?
After the conversion, each page has its own link, such as 'Download page 2 PNG'. Press the link for the page you need. The ZIP is only for downloading all pages at once.
What size are the PNG images?
Each page is rendered at one and a half times its normal size, so the pictures are sharp enough to share or print. They are not full-resolution scans.
Can I get JPG images instead of PNG?
No. This tool only makes PNG images. Use Image Converter afterwards if you need a JPG version of a PNG.
Why does a large PDF take so long?
Every page is drawn in your browser one by one. A long PDF with many pages takes longer, and a very large file may run out of memory. Try a smaller file if it stops.

tools.meta_description: Draw your signature and download it as a PNG, free in your browser. A visual signature for documents and forms.
steps: Draw your signature on the canvas with your mouse or finger.
Press Clear Signature to start again if the drawing looks wrong.
Press Download Signature PNG to save the signature.

content.use: e-Sign lets you draw a signature on a blank canvas and download it as a PNG image, so you can paste it onto a form, a letter or a document. A shop owner signs a delivery note by drawing on a phone screen. A student signs a permission slip and pastes the image into a Word file. An office worker signs a cover letter without printing it. The canvas is 520 by 180 pixels, which is wide enough for a normal signature. Your drawing never leaves your browser, and the downloaded PNG has a plain background you can place over a document.
content.tip: Draw slowly and in one smooth motion for the cleanest line. If the signature looks wrong, press Clear Signature and draw it again. On a phone, use your finger and turn the phone sideways for more room.
content.limit: The signature is a picture only. It is not a legal digital signature and it does not add your signature to a PDF; it downloads a PNG you place yourself. A blank canvas will not download, and the tool shows a message asking you to draw first.
content.example: Drawing a signature on the canvas and pressing Download Signature PNG saves ak-premium-signature.png, ready to paste into a letter.
faq: Can I sign a PDF directly with e-Sign?
No. e-Sign downloads a PNG image of your signature. Open your document, paste the image where the signature goes, and save the document yourself.
Is this a legal digital signature?
No. It is a picture of your handwriting, not a certificate-based digital signature. It works for informal notes and forms, not for documents that need a certified signature.
Can I use e-Sign on my phone?
Yes. Draw on the canvas with your finger. Turn the phone sideways if the canvas feels narrow.
Why does nothing download when I press the button?
The canvas is probably blank. Draw a signature first; the tool refuses to download an empty canvas and asks you to draw.

short.en: Remove the password from a PDF you own.

steps: Choose the protected PDF with the file button.
Type the exact password, including capital letters.
Press Unlock PDF and download the ordinary PDF that opens without a password.

content.use: Unlocking is for a PDF you own and know the password for, but no longer want to type it every time you open it. It is also the way to get a clean copy of a protected file for printing or for a tool that does not accept protected PDFs.
content.tip: Make sure you type the exact password, including capital letters. A wrong password gives a clear wrong-password message, not a broken file.
content.limit: The tool does real standard PDF decryption and keeps the original pages and layout. It does not guess or crack passwords, and it cannot unlock a file whose password you do not know.
content.example: Unlocking a protected fee receipt gives you an ordinary PDF that opens without a password.
faq: Does Unlock remove the password or just show me the text?
It removes the password properly and downloads a normal PDF with the original pages and layout. It is not the old text-only rebuild.
What if the PDF is not protected?
The tool checks first and tells you the PDF is not password-protected, so you do not waste time on a file that does not need unlocking.
Can I unlock a PDF if I forgot the password?
No. The tool needs the exact password you set. It does not guess or crack passwords, so a file with a forgotten password cannot be opened here.
Does unlocking change the file?
No. The pages, text and layout stay exactly as they were. Only the password is removed, so the file opens without asking for it.

tools.meta_description: Unlock a PDF in your browser with the AK Premium Unlock tool. Rebuilds a readable PDF from the file you provide.

short.en: Lock a PDF with a password (AES-256).

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type a password you can remember. There is no way to recover it if you forget it.
Press Protect PDF and download the encrypted file. It opens in any PDF reader with the password.

content.use: Protecting a PDF is for files that should only be opened by someone who knows the password: a salary slip, a contract draft, a fee receipt or a report with personal details. The password travels with the file, so it works in Acrobat and Chrome without any account.
content.tip: Use a password you can remember or store safely, because there is no way to recover it. A password of 8 or more characters with letters and numbers is much harder to guess than a short word.
content.limit: The tool uses standard AES-256 PDF encryption (qpdf, revision 6). It does not stop someone from photographing the screen or re-sharing the file once they have opened it, and a forgotten password cannot be recovered by this site.
content.example: Protecting a salary slip with a password means only the person who knows that password can open it in a PDF reader.
faq: Is this a real PDF password, or a special file only this site can open?
It is a real standard PDF password. The file is a normal .pdf, encrypted with AES-256, and it opens in Acrobat, Chrome and other PDF readers with the password.
What happens if I forget the password?
The file cannot be opened without it. This site does not store your password and cannot reset it, so keep it somewhere safe before you share the file.
How short can the password be?
At least 4 characters. A longer password with letters and numbers is much harder to guess, so use 8 or more characters if you can.
Can I change the password later?
Yes, in two steps. Unlock the file with the old password first, then protect it again with the new password. This tool has no direct change-password button.

tools.meta_description: Protect a PDF with a password in your browser. Files are encrypted locally and only this site's Unlock tool can reopen them.
Crop the margins of every page in a PDF, free in your browser. Tidy page edges without uploading your file.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type the crop margin in points in the 'Crop margin, points' box. The default is 36.
Press Crop PDF and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Crop PDF trims the same margin off every side of every page, which removes wide white borders from scanned pages. A student crops the empty borders off scanned notes so they read better on a phone. An office worker crops the margins off a scanned form before printing it. A teacher crops a worksheet so the questions fill more of the page. You type the margin in points, and the default of 36 points trims about half an inch from each side. The text in the middle of the page is never touched, and your original file stays unchanged.
content.tip: Start with the default 36 points and check the result before you crop more. A bigger number trims more from every side, so a large margin can cut into the text near the edge of the page.
content.limit: The same margin is cut from all four sides of every page. You cannot crop one page only, or crop the top more than the bottom. The margin must be between 0 and 200 points, and each page keeps at least 10 points of width and height.
content.example: Cropping a scanned worksheet with a 36-point margin trims about half an inch of white border from every side of every page.
faq: What is a point?
A point is a printing unit. 72 points make one inch, so the default 36 points is about half an inch of margin on each side.
Can I crop only the top of the page?
No. The same margin is cut from all four sides of every page. To crop one edge only, use a PDF editor that supports free cropping.
Will cropping cut into my text?
It can, if the margin is larger than the white space around your text. Start with 36 points and check the result; raise it slowly if the borders are still wide.
Can I crop a single page?
No. The margin applies to every page in the file. Split the PDF first if only one page needs cropping.

short.en: Permanently cover matching text in black.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type the exact text to redact, including spaces.
Press Redact and download the PDF. Open it in a PDF reader to confirm the covered text cannot be selected.

content.use: Redaction is for removing sensitive details before a document is shared: a CNIC number, a phone number, a bank account number or a name in a report. It is used when a document must be shared but a few details in it must not be seen by anyone.
content.tip: Type the exact text to redact, including spaces. Check the downloaded PDF before you share it, and open it in a PDF reader to confirm the covered text cannot be selected or copied.
content.limit: Redaction works on the text layer of a PDF. Pages that contain a match are rebuilt as images with the black box burned in, so the covered text is gone from those pages. Pages without a match are copied unchanged. A scanned PDF has no text layer, so redact it after OCR, not before.
content.example: Redacting 35202-1234567-1 from a form covers every place that CNIC appears with a black box.
faq: Is the redacted text really gone, or just covered?

It is really gone from the affected pages. Those pages are rebuilt as images with the box burned into the picture, and the original text layer on those pages is destroyed, so the text cannot be selected or copied out.
Can I redact a scanned PDF?
Not directly. A scanned PDF has no text layer to search. Run OCR PDF first to make a text PDF, then redact that copy.
Does the search care about capital letters?
No. The match ignores capitals, so typing cnic finds CNIC and Cnic. It matches part of a word too, so check the result before sharing.
What if the text appears on many pages?
Every page with a match is rebuilt with the black box burned in. Pages without a match are copied unchanged, so the rest of the document stays sharp.

tools.meta_description: Black out matching text in a PDF, free in your browser. Cover sensitive words before you share a document.
Make an archive-style PDF/A copy of your PDF, free in your browser. Adds archive metadata to your file.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type a title in the 'Title' box, or leave it blank to use 'Archive document'.
Press Make Archive Copy and save the downloaded file.

content.use: PDF to PDF/A makes an archive-style copy of a PDF with a title, author and creation information set, so the file is tidier for long-term storage. An office worker archives old reports with a clear title and author. A student archives assignments so they are easy to find years later. A shop owner archives invoices with a proper title instead of a scanner's file name. The tool sets the title you type, marks the author as AK Premium, and re-saves the file in your browser. It does not change the pages themselves, and your original file stays untouched.
content.tip: Type a clear title that says what the file is, such as 'Sales report March 2026', because the title is what shows up in search and in PDF readers. Keep a copy of the original too, in case you need the untouched file later.
content.limit: This is an archive-style copy, not a certified PDF/A validation. The tool only sets the title, author, subject and keywords and re-saves the file. It does not check fonts, colours or embedding rules, and it does not convert scanned images into text.
content.example: Typing 'Invoice March 2026' as the title and pressing Make Archive Copy downloads a copy of the invoice with that title stored in its information.
faq: Is the result a real certified PDF/A file?
No. The tool sets title, author, subject and keywords and re-saves the file, but it does not validate the file against the PDF/A standard. The page itself says so.
What happens if I leave the title blank?
The tool uses 'Archive document' as the title. Type a real title if you want the file to be easy to find later.
Does the tool change my pages?
No. The pages stay exactly as they are. Only the file information, such as the title and author, is set.
Who is listed as the author?
The author is set to AK Premium, because the copy is made by this tool. The title is yours to choose.

short.en: Re-save a damaged PDF, best effort.

tools.meta_description: Try to repair a damaged PDF by re-saving it, free in your browser. Best-effort recovery for files that will not open.
steps: Choose the damaged PDF file with the file button.
Press Repair PDF.
Save the downloaded file, either a re-saved copy or a rebuilt text PDF.

content.use: Repair PDF tries to rescue a PDF that will not open, which happens when a download stops halfway or a file is copied badly. A student repairs an assignment PDF that a portal refuses to open. An office worker repairs a report that shows an error in the reader. A shop owner repairs an invoice that a customer cannot open. The tool first tries to re-save the file as it is. If that fails, it pulls out any readable text and rebuilds a simple text PDF from it. It is a best-effort rescue, so some files cannot be saved, and the tool says so honestly.
content.tip: Keep the damaged original file and work on a copy. If the repair gives you a rebuilt text PDF, check that the important pages and numbers are there before you send it on.
content.limit: Repair is best effort only. A file with no readable content cannot be fixed, and the tool will say it could not repair the file. When it falls back to rebuilding from text, the layout, images, tables and fonts are lost; only the words survive.
content.example: A half-downloaded 8-page report that will not open is repaired by re-saving it, and the download gives back all 8 pages in a working PDF.
faq: What does Repair PDF do first?
It tries to open the file and re-save it unchanged. That fixes files whose structure is slightly broken but whose pages are still there.
What is the rebuilt text PDF?
If re-saving fails, the tool pulls out any readable text and builds a plain new PDF from the words alone. The layout, images and tables are lost, but the text is saved.
Can Repair PDF fix a password-protected file?
No. A protected file must be unlocked first. Repair cannot read a file it cannot open.
Will the repaired file look the same as the original?
Not always. A re-saved copy looks the same, but a rebuilt text PDF is plain text on plain pages. Check the result before you send it.

tools.meta_description: Compare the text in two PDFs and spot the differences, free in your browser. No upload, no sign-up.
steps: Choose the first PDF with the first file button.
Choose the second PDF with the second file button.
Press Compare PDFs and read the two lists shown on the page: lines only in the first PDF, and lines only in the second.

content.use: Compare PDF checks the text in two PDF files and shows you the lines that appear in only one of them, so you can spot what changed between two versions. A teacher compares a draft and a final handout to see which questions changed. An office worker compares last month's report with this month's to find new figures. A student compares two copies of an assignment to find missing paragraphs. The tool reads the text layer of both files, matches the lines, and lists the lines that are only in the first file and the lines that are only in the second file, with a count for each.
content.tip: Compare the same kind of file with the same kind of file, such as two versions of one report. If the PDFs are scans with no text layer, the tool finds no text to compare, so use OCR PDF on them first.
content.limit: The tool compares whole lines of text, not single words, and it only reads PDFs with a text layer. Scanned-image PDFs give no text to compare. The result is shown on the page; it is not downloaded as a file. Lines that moved to a different place but stayed the same are not listed as changed.
content.example: Comparing a 10-page draft with the final version shows 3 lines only in the first PDF and 5 lines only in the second, which are the paragraphs that were added and removed.
faq: Does Compare PDF show me the changed words inside a line?
No. It compares whole lines. If a line changed by one word, the whole old line appears in the first list and the whole new line appears in the second list.
Why does it say no text was found?
One or both PDFs are probably scans with no text layer. Run OCR PDF on the scanned file first, then compare the new text PDF.
Can I download the comparison?
No. The result is shown on the page as two lists. Copy the lists into a document if you need to keep them.
Does the order of the lines matter?
No. The tool matches lines by their text, so a line that moved to another page but stayed the same is not listed as a change.

tools.meta_description: Convert PDF text into Markdown notes, free in your browser. Handy for notes and for working with AI tools.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Convert to Markdown.
Save the downloaded .md file, which you can open in any notes app or editor.

content.use: PDF to Markdown turns the text of a PDF into a Markdown file, so you can paste it into notes apps, wikis and editors that use Markdown. A student turns a chapter into Markdown to keep in a notes app. A developer turns a manual into Markdown to put in a project wiki. A writer turns a report into Markdown to edit it in a plain-text editor. The text is kept page by page, and each page marker becomes a heading in the Markdown file. The result is a plain .md file with no images, tables or fonts, ready to edit anywhere.
content.tip: Open the .md file in your notes app and tidy the headings before you publish it. The page markers become level-two headings, so a long PDF gives you one heading per page to navigate by.
content.limit: Only the text layer is converted. Scanned-image PDFs give no text. Tables, images, fonts and colours are not kept, and the page markers become '## --- Page N ---' headings, which you may want to rename.
content.example: Converting a 6-page manual downloads ak-premium-document.md with the text of all 6 pages, each page under its own '## --- Page N ---' heading.
faq: What is Markdown?
Markdown is plain text with simple marks for headings, lists and links. Notes apps, wikis and code editors read it and turn it into formatted text.
Will my tables come through?
No. Tables become plain lines of text, because the tool only reads the text layer. You will need to rebuild tables by hand in your notes app.
Why does each page start with a heading?
The tool turns the page marker into a level-two heading, such as '## --- Page 2 ---', so you can tell where each page starts. Rename or delete the headings if you do not need them.
Can I convert a scanned PDF to Markdown?
No. A scanned PDF has no text layer to read. Use OCR PDF first to make a text PDF, then convert that file to Markdown.

short.en: Camera photo or image to PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn a camera photo or image into a PDF, free in your browser. Scan a page with your camera and save it as PDF.
steps: Choose a photo with the file button, or take one with your device camera.
Press Make PDF From Photo.
Save the downloaded PDF with your photo on one page.

content.use: Scan to PDF turns a photo of a page into a PDF file, which is the quick way to share a paper document from your phone. A student photographs a handwritten assignment and sends it as a PDF. A shop owner photographs a receipt and keeps it as a PDF record. An office worker photographs a signed form and emails it as a PDF. The photo is centred on an A4 page and saved as a PDF in your browser, so nothing is uploaded. It works with any photo your camera or gallery gives you, and the result is a single-page PDF.
content.tip: Photograph the page straight on, in good light, with the whole page in the frame. A straight, well-lit photo gives a much clearer PDF than a tilted or shadowed one.
content.limit: One photo becomes one PDF page, so several pages need several runs and a merge afterwards. The photo is saved as a picture inside the PDF; the text in it is not readable or searchable. Use OCR PDF afterwards if you need the text.
content.example: Photographing a signed form and pressing Make PDF From Photo downloads ak-premium-scan.pdf with the photo centred on one A4 page.
faq: Can I scan several pages at once?
No. One photo makes one PDF page. Photograph each page, make a PDF for each, then use Merge PDF to join them into one file.
Is the text in my photo searchable?
No. The photo is stored as a picture inside the PDF. To get searchable text, run OCR PDF on the finished PDF.
Does the photo need to be a certain size?
No. Any photo your camera or gallery gives you works. It is fitted to an A4 page automatically, so a very large photo is scaled down.
Can I use the camera directly?
Yes. The file button lets you take a photo with your device camera or pick one from your gallery, depending on your phone or browser.

short.en: Read scanned pages and save them as a text PDF.

tools.meta_description: Read scanned PDF pages as text and save a text PDF, free in your browser. Needs a first-run language download.
steps: Choose a scanned PDF file with the file button.
Press OCR PDF and wait. The first run downloads English language data, and large files take time.
Save the downloaded text PDF when the status says it is done.

content.use: OCR PDF reads the words printed on scanned pages and builds a new PDF from that text, so a scan you could only look at becomes a file you can search and copy from. A student turns scanned textbook pages into searchable text. An office worker turns a scanned contract into text that can be copied. A researcher turns old scanned papers into text for searching. The tool draws each page as a picture, reads the English print with Tesseract in your browser, and writes the recognised words into a fresh PDF. The first run downloads the English language data, so it takes longer the first time.
content.tip: Use clear, straight scans for the best result. OCR works well on clean printed English and badly on handwriting, faint print or tilted pages. Run it once and check a page before you OCR a very long file.
content.limit: OCR reads English printed text only, and it needs to download language data on the first run. Handwriting, low-quality photos and tilted pages give poor results. Large PDFs take a long time because each page is read one by one, and the new PDF holds text, not the original page pictures.
content.example: Running OCR PDF on a 3-page scanned letter downloads a new PDF with the letter's words as selectable text you can copy.
faq: Why does the first run take so long?
The tool downloads the English OCR language data the first time you use it. Later runs are faster because the data is already there.
Can OCR read handwriting?
Not reliably. OCR is built for clear printed text. Handwriting, faint print and tilted pages give poor or wrong results.
Does OCR keep the layout of my scanned page?
No. The result is a fresh text PDF with the recognised words. The original page pictures, layout and fonts are not kept.
Can OCR read Urdu or other languages?
No. This tool reads English text only. A scan in another language will give wrong or empty text.

tools.meta_description: Make a fillable form PDF with text fields and checkboxes, free in your browser. No sign-up needed.
steps: Type a title for your form in the 'Form title' box, or leave it blank.
Press Create Fillable PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, then open it in a PDF reader and fill in the fields.

content.use: PDF Forms creates a one-page fillable PDF with fields people can type into, so you can collect the same information from everyone in the same format. A teacher makes a simple application form for students. A shop owner makes a feedback form for customers. An office worker makes a request form for staff. The form has a name field, an email field, a checkbox and a dropdown, all on one A4 page with your title at the top. Anyone can open the PDF in a reader, type into the fields, tick the box and pick from the dropdown, then save or print it.
content.tip: Keep the form title short and clear, such as 'Job Application Form', because it is printed large at the top of the page. Test the downloaded PDF in your own PDF reader before you share it, to make sure the fields work there.
content.limit: The form is always the same one-page layout: a name field, an email field, one checkbox and one dropdown. You cannot add, remove or rename fields, and the dropdown choices are fixed. The PDF must be opened in a reader that supports fillable forms.
content.example: Typing 'Customer Feedback Form' and pressing Create Fillable PDF downloads a one-page PDF with that title and four fillable fields ready to use.
faq: What fields does the form have?
A name field, an email field, a checkbox labelled Agree, and a dropdown labelled Category. The layout is fixed and always on one A4 page.
Can I add more fields to the form?
No. The form always has the same four fields. If you need a custom form, build it in a full PDF editor and use this tool for simple forms only.
What title is used if I leave the box blank?
The tool uses 'Application Form' as the title. Type your own title if you want the form to say what it is for.
Will the form work in any PDF reader?
It works in readers that support fillable forms, such as Adobe Reader and most modern browsers. Very old readers may show the fields but not let you type in them.

tools.meta_description: Summarize a PDF in your browser with key sentences picked locally. No file is sent to an external AI service.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Set the number of sentences you want in the 'Sentences' box. The default is 5.
Press Summarize PDF and read the key sentences shown on the page.

content.use: Local Summarizer picks the most important sentences from a PDF and shows them as a short list, so you can grasp a long document in a minute. A student reads the key sentences of a chapter before an exam. An office worker skims a long report to find what matters. A researcher checks whether a paper is worth reading in full. The tool counts which words appear most often in the document and ranks the sentences by those words, then shows the top sentences in order of importance. No AI server is used, and the text never leaves your browser.
content.tip: Start with 5 sentences for a quick overview, and raise the number to 10 for a longer document. The summary is a list of the document's own sentences, so read it as a guide and open the full PDF for the details.
content.limit: The summary is picked by word frequency, not by understanding. It only uses sentences longer than 30 characters, and it works on PDFs with a text layer only; scanned PDFs give no text to summarise. The summary is shown on the page and is not downloaded as a file.
content.example: Summarising a 20-page report with 5 sentences shows the 5 most important sentences from the whole document, ranked by the words that appear most often.
faq: Is this an AI summary?
No. No AI server is used. The tool counts the most frequent words in the document and picks the sentences that contain them most, all in your browser.
Why does it only show 5 sentences?
The Sentences box defaults to 5. You can set any number from 1 to 10 before you press Summarize PDF.
Can I summarise a scanned PDF?
No. A scanned PDF has no text layer, so the tool finds nothing to summarise. Run OCR PDF on it first, then summarise the new text PDF.
Is the summary downloaded as a file?
No. The key sentences are shown on the page as a list. Copy them into your notes if you want to keep them.

tools.meta_description: Extract PDF text ready to translate, free in your browser. It prepares the text; translation itself happens elsewhere.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Extract Text for Translation.
Save the downloaded .txt file and translate it in a service of your choice.

content.use: Translate Helper pulls the text out of a PDF into a plain .txt file, ready for you to translate in a service you choose. A student extracts a chapter to translate it into Urdu. An office worker extracts a notice to translate it for staff. A shop owner extracts a price list to translate it for customers. The tool does not translate anything itself, because automatic translation would need to send your text to an outside service. Instead it gives you clean text, grouped by page, that you can paste into any translation app you trust.
content.tip: Translate the .txt file in small parts, because translation apps handle short passages better than a whole book at once. Keep the page markers in the text so you can match the translation back to the original pages.
content.limit: The tool extracts text only; it does not translate. It only reads PDFs with a text layer, so scanned PDFs give no text. The text comes out as plain lines, so tables and layout are not kept.
content.example: Extracting a 2-page notice downloads ak-premium-for-translation.txt with the notice text, grouped by page, ready to paste into a translation app.
faq: Does this tool translate my PDF?
No. It extracts the text into a .txt file. You translate that text in a service you choose, such as Google Translate or DeepL.
Why does the tool not translate directly?
Automatic translation needs an outside service, which would send your text off your browser. To keep your files local, this tool only extracts the text.
Can I extract text from a scanned PDF?
No. A scanned PDF has no text layer. Use OCR PDF first to make a text PDF, then run Translate Helper on the new file.
What does the .txt file look like?
Plain text grouped by page, with a '--- Page N ---' marker before each page. The layout, images and tables are not kept.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
If the PDF is a scan, tick the OCR option first.
Press Convert and download the .xlsx file, then check a few cells before trusting a total.

content.use: Converting a PDF to Excel is for getting numbers out of a PDF table: a bank statement, a price list, a stock report or a fee table that needs to be sorted, totalled or charted. Once the numbers are in Excel, formulas can work on them.
content.tip: Tables with clear gaps between columns convert best. If a table has no gaps, the whole line lands in one cell and you can use Text to Columns in Excel to split it.
content.limit: Columns are detected from the gaps between words on each line. Tables with merged cells, no gaps or rotated text may not split cleanly, and numbers are stored as text in some cases, so check a few cells before you trust a total.
content.example: A price list PDF with item, quantity and price columns becomes a spreadsheet with those three columns.
faq: Why did my table land in one column?
The PDF had no clear gap between its columns, so the tool kept the whole line together. In Excel, select the column, use Data, Text to Columns, and split on spaces or a delimiter.
Are the numbers in my Excel file real numbers?
They are text in most cases, because a PDF does not say whether a word is a number. In Excel, select the column and use Paste Special, Values, or multiply by 1 to turn text numbers into real numbers.
What file do I download?
A spreadsheet named ak-premium-pdf-to-excel.xlsx. The extracted text goes on a sheet called Extracted Text, with a title row at the top.
Can I convert two PDFs at once?
No. Choose one PDF at a time. Convert the first file, download the spreadsheet, then choose the next PDF and convert it the same way.

tools.meta_description: Turn extracted PDF text into an .xlsx spreadsheet, free in your browser. Text-based conversion, layout is not preserved.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
If the PDF is a scan, tick the OCR option first, otherwise the tool finds no text.
Press Convert and download the .docx file.

content.use: Converting a PDF to Word is for editing a document that only exists as a PDF: a letter, a report or a form that needs changes. The Word file can then be edited, spell-checked and printed like any other document.
content.tip: If the PDF is a scan, tick the OCR option before converting. Otherwise the tool will find no text to convert and will tell you so.
content.limit: Paragraphs are rebuilt from the text positions in the PDF, so headings, plain paragraphs and simple tables usually survive. Original fonts, exact spacing, images, charts and complex tables are not preserved. This is a text reconstruction, not a pixel-perfect copy.
content.example: A 2-page letter becomes a Word document with the same paragraphs in the same order, ready to edit.
faq: Will my Word file look exactly like the PDF?
No. It keeps the text and paragraph order, and short first lines are treated as headings, but fonts, spacing and images are not carried over. For exact appearance, keep the PDF.
What if my PDF is a scanned image?
Tick the OCR option. The tool reads the scanned pages with text recognition first, then builds the Word file from that text. Handwriting and blurry scans give poor results.
Does the Word file keep page breaks from the PDF?
No. The text flows as one continuous document. The paragraphs stay in order, but the page breaks from the PDF are not carried over.
What Word file do I get?
A Word document named ak-premium-pdf-to-word.docx. It opens in Microsoft Word, Google Docs and other word processors, and you can edit it like any normal Word file.

tools.meta_description: Turn extracted PDF text into a .docx document, free in your browser. Text-based conversion, layout is not preserved.
Turn extracted PDF text into a .pptx presentation, free in your browser. Text-based conversion, layout is not preserved.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Convert PDF to PPT.
Save the downloaded .pptx file, which has one slide per PDF page.

content.use: PDF to PPT turns each page of a PDF into a slide in a PowerPoint file, so you can present or edit the words from a document. A teacher turns a handout into slides for a lesson. A student turns a report into slides for a class presentation. An office worker turns a briefing into slides for a meeting. The first line of each page becomes the slide title in large bold text, and the rest of the page becomes the slide body. The file downloads as a .pptx that opens in PowerPoint and other slide apps. The layout, images and charts from the PDF are not kept, only the words.
content.tip: Check the slides after the conversion and tidy the titles, because the first line of a page is not always a real heading. Add your own pictures and charts in PowerPoint afterwards, since the tool only brings the words across.
content.limit: The conversion is text-only. Layout, fonts, tables, images, charts and animations are not preserved. Each PDF page becomes one slide, with the first line as the title and the rest as body text. A scanned PDF with no text layer cannot be converted and the tool says so.
content.example: Converting a 5-page briefing downloads ak-premium-pdf-to-ppt.pptx with 5 slides, one per page, each with a title and body text.
faq: How does the tool choose the slide title?
It takes the first line of text on each page and makes it the slide title in large bold text. The rest of the page becomes the body text.
Will my images and charts come across?
No. The conversion is text-only. Images, charts, tables and animations are left behind. Add them to the slides in PowerPoint afterwards.
What if my PDF is a scan?
The tool will say no readable text was found. Run OCR PDF first to make a text PDF, then convert that file to PPT.
Can I open the file in Google Slides?
Yes. The .pptx file opens in PowerPoint, Google Slides, LibreOffice Impress and other apps that read PowerPoint files.

tools.meta_description: Paste text or HTML and download it as a PDF, free in your browser. No upload, no sign-up.
steps: Paste your text or simple HTML into the box.
Press Convert Text to PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF.

content.use: TXT / HTML to PDF turns pasted text into a PDF file, which is handy when you have words in a message, a note or a web page and need them as a document. A student pastes an essay draft and downloads it as a PDF to submit. An office worker pastes a notice from an email and saves it as a PDF. A shop owner pastes a price list from a chat and sends it as a PDF. Any HTML tags in the pasted text are stripped out, so the result is plain text in a simple 12-point font, flowing across pages as needed. Nothing is uploaded; the PDF is built in your browser.
content.tip: Paste the text, then check it in the box before you convert, because the tool strips HTML tags and extra spaces. For a clean result, paste plain text rather than copied web page formatting.
content.limit: HTML tags are stripped and formatting is not kept. The PDF is plain 12-point text only, with no bold, headings, images or tables. Very long text flows across pages automatically, but you cannot choose the font, size or page layout.
content.example: Pasting a 300-word notice and pressing Convert Text to PDF downloads ak-premium-text-to-pdf.pdf with the notice as plain text on one page.
faq: Does the tool keep my HTML formatting?
No. All HTML tags are stripped out and the text becomes plain 12-point text. Use it for simple text, not for formatted web pages.
What happens to very long text?
It flows across pages automatically. The tool adds pages as needed, so a long paste becomes a multi-page PDF.
Can I paste from a Word document?
Yes, but only the words come through. Bold, headings, tables and images from Word are dropped, and the text becomes plain 12-point text.
Is my pasted text uploaded anywhere?
No. The PDF is built in your browser with jsPDF. The text never leaves your device.

content.use: Converting Excel to PDF is for sharing a sheet that must not be changed: a price list, a report, or a table for a client. The PDF shows the numbers as they are, without formulas.
content.tip: Check that the first sheet is the one you want, because only the first sheet is converted. Keep the sheet simple for the best result.
content.limit: This is a basic text conversion. Only the first sheet is rendered, as plain text rows. Cell colours, formulas, charts and multiple sheets are not preserved.
content.example: A price list sheet becomes a PDF with each row on its own line.
faq: Why is only the first sheet converted?
This basic conversion reads the first sheet only. If you need another sheet, move it to the front in Excel and convert again.
Are the formulas in my Excel file kept?
No. The PDF shows the values, not the formulas. The numbers are what you see in the sheet.
What Excel files can I upload?
Both .xlsx and .xls files. Choose the file, press Convert Excel to PDF, and the tool reads the first sheet.
Does the PDF keep the column layout?
No. Each row becomes a line of plain text, so columns are not lined up like a spreadsheet. Keep the sheet simple for the cleanest result.

tools.meta_description: Render the first sheet of an Excel file as a PDF, free in your browser. Your spreadsheet never leaves your device.
steps: Choose an Excel file (.xlsx or .xls) with the file button.
Press Convert Excel to PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, which holds the first sheet as plain text rows.

content.use: Converting Word to PDF is for sending a document that must look the same everywhere: a CV, a letter, or a form. A PDF cannot be edited by mistake, and it opens on any phone or computer.
content.tip: Keep the Word file simple. Headings, lists and tables survive, but complex formatting, images and tracked changes do not.
content.limit: This is a basic text conversion. Headings, lists and tables are kept where the structure allows, but fonts, images, headers, footers and exact page layout are not preserved.
content.example: A simple Word letter becomes a PDF with the same paragraphs in the same order.
faq: Is this a full Word to PDF conversion?
No. It is a basic text conversion. It keeps the text, headings, lists and tables where possible, but not the exact layout, fonts or images.
What if my Word file has images?
Images are not carried into the PDF by this basic conversion. For a document with images, use Word itself to save as PDF.
Can I convert an old .doc file?
No. The tool only accepts .docx files. If your file is a .doc, open it in Word and save it as .docx first.
Does it keep tracked changes?
No. Tracked changes and comments are not carried into the PDF. Accept the changes in Word first if you want the final text.

tools.meta_description: Render Word document text as a PDF, free in your browser. Text-based rendering, layout is not preserved.
steps: Choose a Word (.docx) file with the file button.
Press Convert Word to PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, which holds the document text in plain 12-point text.

content.use: Converting PowerPoint to PDF is for sharing slides that must look the same on any device, or for printing a deck without PowerPoint. A PDF is also easier to attach to an email than a large presentation file.
content.tip: Keep the slides simple. The tool reads the text on each slide, one slide per PDF page.
content.limit: This is a basic text conversion. Only the slide text is carried over. Slide designs, images, charts, animations and transitions are not preserved.
content.example: A 5-slide deck becomes a 5-page PDF with the text from each slide.
faq: Is this a full PowerPoint to PDF conversion?
No. It is a basic, text-only conversion. Designs, images and animations are not carried over.
What if a slide has no text?
That slide becomes a page that says there is no text on the slide, so the page count still matches the deck.
Can I convert an old .ppt file?
No. The tool only accepts .pptx files. Open the deck in PowerPoint and save it as .pptx first, then convert the new file.
Does each slide become one PDF page?
Yes. The tool reads the text on each slide and puts it on its own page, so a 5-slide deck becomes a 5-page PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn PowerPoint slide text into a PDF, free in your browser. Basic slide text as PDF, layout is not preserved.
steps: Choose a PowerPoint (.pptx) file with the file button.
Press Convert PPT to PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, which holds the text from each slide.
Pick the task from the list, for example SUMIF or VLOOKUP.
Fill in the labelled fields with your own ranges and values.
Press Generate, copy the formula and paste it into Excel, then test it on a copy of your data.

content.use: An Excel formula generator is for the everyday spreadsheet jobs that are easy to describe but hard to write from memory: adding up sales for one city, counting approved orders, or looking up a price from another sheet. It turns a plain description into a formula you can paste.
content.tip: Pick the task first, then fill in the labelled fields with your own ranges. The formula is built from exactly what you typed, so double-check the ranges before you paste it into Excel.
content.limit: The tool builds formulas from fixed templates, not from AI. It does not read your workbook and cannot guess your cell addresses. Always test a formula on a copy of your data first.
content.example: Choosing SUMIF, entering B2:B20 as the range to add, A2:A20 as the range to check, and Lahore as the condition gives =SUMIF(A2:A20, "Lahore", B2:B20).
faq: Is this AI?
No. The tool uses fixed, parameterized templates. You pick the task and fill in the fields, and it builds the exact formula from those values. It does not guess or learn from your data.
Why does my formula show an error in Excel?
The most common reason is a range that does not exist in your sheet, or a sheet name that needs quotes. Check the ranges, and test on a copy of your data.
Which formulas can it build?
Eleven. SUMIF, SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX plus MATCH, IF, Nested IF, TEXT, DATEDIF and UNIQUE. Pick one from the Task list.
Does it explain the formula too?
Yes. The result shows the formula, a plain-language explanation of what each part does, and an example you can follow.

tools.meta_description: Generate Excel formulas from a plain-words description, free in your browser. Describe the task, get the formula.
Paste an Excel formula and understand what it does, free in your browser. A plain-words explanation, step by step.
steps: Paste a formula that starts with = in the 'Formula' box, for example =VLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!A:B, 2, FALSE).
Press Explain Formula.
Read the explanation in the box below, which lists each function found and what it does.

content.use: Formula Explainer reads an Excel formula and explains it in plain words, so you can understand a formula someone else wrote or check your own work. A student pastes a VLOOKUP from a class example to learn what each part does. An office worker pastes a SUMIF from a shared report to see why the total looks wrong. A shop owner pastes an IF formula from a price sheet to understand the condition. The tool lists the functions it finds and explains each one from its dictionary, then gives a plain-language reading of the whole formula. It does not run the formula or check your numbers; it explains what the formula says.
content.tip: Paste the full formula including the = sign, or the tool will ask you to. If a function is not in the dictionary, the tool says so; check Excel help for that function's exact arguments.
content.limit: The tool explains 8 functions only: SUM, IF, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH, COUNTIF and SUMIF. Any other function gets a note that it is not in the dictionary yet. The tool does not run the formula, check your cell references or test it against your data.
content.example: Pasting =VLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!A:B, 2, FALSE) explains that VLOOKUP searches the first column of a table and returns a value from a column to its right.
faq: Which functions can the tool explain?
Eight: SUM, IF, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH, COUNTIF and SUMIF. Other functions get a note that they are not in the dictionary yet.
Does the tool run my formula?
No. It reads the formula and explains what each part does. It does not open your workbook or check whether the result is correct.
Why does it say my formula must start with =?
Excel formulas start with an equals sign. Paste the whole formula, including the =, or the tool cannot read it.
Can I use the explanation in my work?
Yes. The explanation is plain text you can read and learn from. Always test the formula on a copy of your data before you use it in a real sheet.

content.use: A VBA macro writer is for repeating a job in Excel without doing it by hand every time: marking rows that meet a condition, copying data to a report sheet, filtering a table, or hiding a settings sheet. The macro does the clicks for you.
content.tip: Start with a small task, such as looping through rows, and test the macro on a copy of your workbook. Press Alt + F11 in Excel, insert a module, paste the code, and run it from there.
content.limit: The tool builds macros from fixed templates. It does not write a macro for a job it has no template for, and it cannot test the macro against your workbook. Macros only run in Excel for Windows or Mac with macros enabled.
content.example: Choosing Loop through rows, with sheet Data, column A and the condition over 100, gives a macro that marks those rows High in column B.
faq: How do I run the macro in Excel?
Press Alt + F11, insert a module, paste the code, close the editor, then press Alt + F8 and run the macro. Save the file as .xlsm if you want to keep the macro.
Is the macro safe to run?
Read it first. It only does what the template says: it works on the sheet and range you entered. Test it on a copy of your workbook before you run it on real data.
Which macros can it write?
Five. Loop through rows, copy data to another sheet, AutoFilter a table, sort a table, and hide a sheet so it is very hidden. Pick one from the Task list.
Does it work in Google Sheets?
No. VBA only runs in Excel on Windows or Mac. Google Sheets uses a different language, so paste the code in Excel instead.

tools.meta_description: Write Excel VBA macros from a plain-words description, free in your browser. Describe the automation, get VBA code.
steps: Pick a task in the 'Task' list: Loop through rows, Copy data to another sheet, AutoFilter a table, Sort a table, or Hide a sheet (very hidden).
Fill in the labelled fields that appear for that task.
Press Generate and copy the VBA code from the box below.

content.use: A regex creator is for finding or checking a pattern in text: an email address, a Pakistan mobile number, a CNIC, a date, or a web link. It is used in spreadsheets, text editors and data cleaning, where a pattern is faster than reading every line.
content.tip: Paste some of your own text in the test box and press Generate. The tool shows you exactly which parts matched, so you can see if the pattern is right before you use it anywhere else.
content.limit: The tool gives you a fixed pattern for a named task. It does not build a pattern for a new, unusual format, and a pattern that matches your test text may still miss a different format of the same thing.
content.example: Choosing Pakistan mobile number gives 03\d{2}[- ]?\d{7}, which finds 0300-1234567 and 03001234567.
faq: What is a regex?
A regular expression is a short pattern that describes a shape of text, such as an email address. A program can then find every piece of text with that shape.
Can I use this pattern in Excel?
Yes, with VBA, or in Google Sheets with REGEXEXTRACT. Paste the pattern exactly as shown, including the backslashes.
Which patterns can it create?
Six. Email address, Pakistan mobile number, date in DD/MM/YYYY form, web link, numbers in text, and Pakistan CNIC. Pick one from the Pattern list.
Can I test the pattern on my own text?
Yes. Paste text in the test box and press Generate. The tool shows which parts matched, so you can check the pattern before you use it.

tools.meta_description: Build regex patterns and extract emails and dates, free in your browser. Describe the pattern, get working regex.
steps: Pick a pattern in the 'Pattern for' list: Email address, Pakistan mobile number, Date (DD/MM/YYYY), Web link, Numbers in text, or Pakistan CNIC.
Paste some text in the 'Test text' box if you want to test the pattern.
Press Generate Pattern and copy the pattern from the box below.

short.en: Describe it, get a DAX measure.

content.use: A DAX measure is for Power BI and Excel Power Pivot: a total, an average, a year-to-date figure, or a share of the total that updates when a user filters the report. It is the calculation behind most Power BI cards and charts.
content.tip: Use your real table and column names in the fields. The measure name is the name that will appear in your report, so make it clear, such as Total Sales.
content.limit: The tool builds measures from fixed templates. It does not connect to your Power BI file and cannot check that your table or column names are right. Paste the measure into Power BI and test it there.
content.example: Choosing Total Sales, with table Sales and column Amount, gives Total Sales = SUM(Sales[Amount]).
faq: What is DAX?
DAX is the formula language of Power BI and Excel Power Pivot. A measure is a calculation, such as a total, that is worked out when a user looks at the report.
Why does my measure show an error in Power BI?
The table or column name is usually the reason. Check the spelling and the square brackets, and make sure the table exists in your model.
Which measures can it build?
Five. Total Sales, Average, Year to Date, Percent of Total, and Count Rows. Pick one from the Task list and fill in your table and column names.
Do I need Power BI to use it?
No. The same measures also work in Excel Power Pivot. Paste the measure into either one, with your own table and column names.

tools.meta_description: Write DAX measures for Power BI from a plain-words description, free in your browser. Describe the measure, get DAX.
steps: Pick a measure in the 'Task' list: Total Sales, Average, Year to Date, Percent of Total, or Count Rows.
Fill in the labelled fields with your table and column names.
Press Generate, then copy the DAX measure and paste it into Power BI or Excel Power Pivot.

tools.meta_description: Export the first sheet of an Excel file as CSV, free in your browser. Your file never leaves your device.
steps: Choose an Excel file (.xlsx or .xls) with the file button.
Press Convert Excel to CSV.
Save the downloaded .csv file, which holds the first sheet of your workbook.

content.use: Excel to CSV exports the first sheet of an Excel workbook as a plain .csv file, so the data can be opened in other apps or uploaded to a system that only takes CSV. A shop owner exports a stock list to upload to an online store. An office worker exports a customer list to import into another program.
